paper_metadata.title: Quantum algorithm for calculating risk contributions in a credit portfolio

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based quantum algorithm for CVaR contribution estimation in a single-factor Merton credit portfolio model, using simultaneous multiple-expected-value estimation plus fixed-point QAA. The main theoretical result is query complexity eO((sigma_max / (epsilon * sqrt(p))) * log(max(Cmax/epsilon, Emax/sigma_max)) * log(Ngr/delta)), compared with classical Monte Carlo eTheta(sigma_max^2 log(Ngr/delta)/(epsilon^2 p)); the paper emphasizes quadratic speedup in epsilon but no asymptotic speedup in the number of groups Ngr.

experiments.description: Quantum algorithm for estimating CVaR risk contributions of multiple obligor groups in a credit portfolio under the Merton model, using simultaneous multiple-expected-value estimation and fixed-point quantum amplitude amplification.

algorithm.variant: Quantum multiple expected value estimation for CVaR contributions with fixed-point QAA

hyperparameters.Cmax: upper bound on group CVaR contributions
hyperparameters.sigma_max: upper bound on conditional standard deviations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Standard normal random variable is discretized into an amplitude-encoded state |SN>; obligor defaults are generated via controlled Y rotations from default probabilities Pdef_k(x); group losses are computed by arithmetic on the default indicators.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate CVaR contributions C_v^K = E[L_K | L >= v] for K in [Ngr] in the Merton credit portfolio model.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Condition L >= v is handled by fixed-point quantum amplitude amplification and post-selection on the marked ancilla qubit.

problem_instance.description: Credit portfolio risk-management instance in the single-factor Merton model with obligors partitioned into Ngr groups.

dataset_specification.description: Single systematic factor X0 and idiosyncratic factors X1..XNobl; exposures e1..eNobl, thresholds z1..zNobl, correlations ak.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Standard normal distribution discretized into finite register states; default probabilities computed from the standard normal CDF; no empirical dataset used.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper provides theoretical complexity analysis and asymptotic comparison with classical Monte Carlo; no numerical benchmark experiments are reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of default probabilities, arithmetic subroutines, and bounds Cmax and sigma_max are assumed available.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure the output of QEstimator to obtain approximations of the CVaR contributions.

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic in epsilon; no asymptotic speedup in Ngr
speedup_claims.conditions: for CVaR contribution estimation under the single-factor Merton model, using simultaneous multiple-expected-value estimation and fixed-point QAA
speedup_claims.caveats: Quantum complexity scales as eO(sqrt(Ngr/epsilon)) in the paper's notation and includes 1/sqrt(p) and logarithmic factors; the paper emphasizes that the advantage is reduced as the number of groups Ngr increases.

speedup_claims.conditions: when comparing the proposed quantum method against classical Monte Carlo for multiple group CVaR contributions
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper also states the classical method has better dependence on Ngr, namely eO(log(Ngr)/epsilon^2).

speedup_claims.conditions: rough complexity comparison, ignoring logarithmic factors
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a rough criterion, not an empirical benchmark.

speedup_claims.factor: smaller than classical in some plausible setting; example order of magnitude 10^8 on the left-hand side of the crossover condition
speedup_claims.conditions: extreme case of individual-obligor CVaR contributions with p = 0.01, pdef ~ 0.01, and Cmax/epsilon ~ 0.01
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a back-of-the-envelope estimate, not a numerical experiment.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: eO(log(Ngr)/epsilon^2) for classical Monte Carlo estimation of all group contributions; detailed sample complexity also given as eTheta(sigma_max^2 log(Ngr/delta)/(epsilon^2 p)).

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established experimentally; paper gives only asymptotic comparison and a rough condition (sigma_max^2)/(epsilon^2 p) >> Ngr.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require fault-tolerant logical qubits, high-fidelity arithmetic, state preparation for the standard normal distribution, and amplitude estimation subroutines; no hardware resource estimate is provided.
limiting_factors: No hardware experiment or simulator benchmark is reported
Only theoretical query complexity is analyzed
Quantum advantage is only quadratic in epsilon and reduced as Ngr grows
State preparation and arithmetic subroutines dominate practical cost
Classical Monte Carlo has better dependence on Ngr

notes: No numerical hardware experiment is reported; hardware is not specified because the paper is purely theoretical.
num_qubits and circuit depth are not explicitly stated as fixed values; they depend on Ngr, Nobl, and the precision register size Ndig, so they are left null/inferred only at the symbolic level.
The paper explicitly states the asymptotic quantum and classical complexities and argues there is no asymptotic speedup in Ngr, only quadratic speedup in epsilon.
The paper is a purely theoretical proposal for CVaR contribution estimation in a credit portfolio.

It reports asymptotic quantum complexity eO((sigma_max / (epsilon * sqrt(p))) * log(max(Cmax/epsilon, Emax/sigma_max)) * log(Ngr/delta)) and classical complexity eTheta(sigma_max^2 log(Ngr/delta)/(epsilon^2 p)), but no empirical benchmark.
